title: Cocktails
text: “Ohh? Iwatani-sama’s cocktails? I really must give one a try, indeed.”
“Vōfu! Wanna drink!”
“Ah, what sort of thing is it?”
The slaves, their eyes already growing a bit glazed from drink, asked Father.
“I could probably recreate quite a few. Well, rather than have you all get sloppy drunk chugging away, maybe I should whip something up to help settle you down for a bit. Got any tools for that?”

When Father asked one of the servants, they scrambled off in a fluster to gather tools from the kitchen and the tavern in the territory. Meanwhile, Wolf and the others just kept right on drinking. Eventually the tools and ice arrived.
“Well then, guess I’ll make some cocktails.”
Crack, crack, crack—he deftly chipped away at the ice with an ice pick.
“Ohh, booze is outside my old man’s jurisdiction too, so this is a surprise.”
“Well, Lars-chan’s dad is more the food type. Though it’s not like he doesn’t know anything about it. He probably just still thinks of Lars-chan as a kid.”
“Keh! I’m already an adult, y’know!”
Clink, clink—with practiced ease he set to work on the first cocktail, making it for Panda.
“You’re already past dinner, so maybe I’ll start with something standard.”
He filled a cup with ice to chill it, poured in several kinds of liquor, and quietly stirred it with a spoon. Eventually he transferred it into another cup—or a proper glass, rather—and held it out.
“Here. A pretend martini. Simple, to start.”
“Aye.”
Panda took the cocktail and brought it to her lips, and her face lit up with surprise.
“Pretty strong, but tastes good. The kind of flavor you didn’t know you wanted until right now.”
“Figured you looked like you wanted something dry, so I gave it a shot. Glad it worked. Refreshing too, huh?”
“Yeah, yeah. Geez, you’re just as good at reading people as my old man.”
While Panda sipped away little by little at Father’s special cocktail, Father moved on to the next task.
“Next... guess I’ll do Wolf?”
“Vōfu.”
“Wolf seems to like sweet stuff, and he looks like he wants it fast.”
So he poured it into a shaker and, with practiced rhythm, shook it—clack clack clack—before quietly pouring it into a glass.
“Here. Something like an Alexander.”

He set it down smoothly. Alexander—was that a reference to the Great King? Surely not. I couldn’t tell at a glance what liquor was in it. But I had a feeling this was something Father often made for Older Sister. I’d sampled plenty of Father’s cooking myself, but I’d never really paid much mind to his drinks. Come to think of it, he always seemed to serve these as a matter of course whenever dealing with Older Sister and her lot. A method for getting them thoroughly plastered, perhaps?
“Vof! Oh, sweet!”
Wolf downed it in one big gulp. Surely a strong drink, the kind that would hit hard later. Father really is a cunning one, indeed.
“So, next is Theo, I guess? You’re probably not too used to drinking, huh.”
“Iwatani-sama, please make me something that suits me.”
He gave a rather flashy snap of his fingers and pointed at Father. Hmph, what exactly is he trying to decide there?
“Ahaha.”
Father, with a bit of a wry laugh, made and served up a layered cocktail. He worked so deftly it came together in no time.
“Ohh, what a lovely cocktail, indeed.”
It was just like the kind of cocktail I’d pictured as a child.
“It looks just like a melon cream soda, I say.”
There was a clear layer in the middle, green on the bottom and white on top.
“Haha, well, the colors probably do make it look that way. It’s something like a Grasshopper.”
“It’s pretty.”
And for some reason, there were two of them.
“One’s for you too, Motoyasu-kun.”
“So I’m paired with this guy, huh…”
As if the rabbit connection explained everything, Rabbit Guy shot me a look.
“Yuki-chan had this look like she wanted me to hurry up and serve Motoyasu-kun too, so, you know, I just figured.”
“Understood, indeed!”

And so, I got my own serving too. Father’s homemade cocktail—guess I’ll sip it slowly, bit by bit. That was the plan, but… it was made so beautifully that it almost felt like a waste to even put my lips to it. The layers were so crisp and clean that if I’d had a camera, I would have wanted to snap a picture—it was that well made, I say.
“Ah, if you wanted to drink from your favorite layer first, I probably should’ve provided straws… guess I messed up a little there.”
“I focused too much on looks and went with a pousse-café style,” Father apologized.
“No need to worry about it.”
Rabbit Guy smoothly drank Father’s cocktail, as artful as it was.
“Ah, this is nice. It’s got this fruity flavor, just like juice. Is this even alcohol?”
“I picked something easy to drink, after all.”

I drank mine too. Ohh… it reminded me of something I’d had back when I was in Japan, but this one had a far more distinct, solid flavor along with a stronger aroma. What I recalled was something like a chocolate mint drink, but this one was much more refreshing.
“Vofuu… he’s making all sorts of things with whatever liquor’s on hand.”
“Well, I’ve got a little trick—I use drop items for flavoring too.”
Father chuckled softly as he added the supplementary detail while finishing up the cocktail. Was that really such an easy thing to do?
“So then, what should I make for Shion, who’s been waiting so patiently? Any requests?”
“Not really sure. I haven’t drunk enough to know.”
“Well, if anything, it’s more like Lars-chan, Elmelo-san, and Sadeena-san are the ones among us who’d actually know their liquor brands.”
“What’s up with it being all women?”
Come to think of it, that was true.
“Gaelion-chan and the other dragons probably know a thing or two as well, given how long they’ve lived.”
“Rival wouldn’t know a thing, I say.”
Wouldn’t just getting drunk be enough for it? I couldn’t imagine it having such a refined hobby.
“Surprisingly, it seemed to drink a fair bit. Well, Sadeena-san’s such a heavy drinker that it probably just fades into the background by comparison.”
So saying, Father made and served a cocktail for Crocodile Guy.
“For Shion, let’s try something like a Cleopatra. Made the strength similar too. Also known as an Arabian Nights. Something about looking at Shion just makes me think of that crocodile-type god.”
“I’ll take it, then… hm? There’s a flavor like tea, or tea-cakes.”
“Yeah. Probably the rum-like liquor giving you that impression.”
Everyone took a nice swig to cleanse their palate. It was, after all, Father’s own special cocktail.
“It’s delicious. This was a great break in the middle of our drink comparisons.”
“As for what’s left… let’s see, there’s also a cocktail I had here in this world. One I drank at a tavern in Lute Village.”
“Did you ask for the recipe?”
“Well, sort of.”
Shake, shake, shake—he deftly made yet another cocktail. Father really is skilled when it comes to food and drink, indeed.
“Not just cooking, but you know your liquor too, huh.”
“I told you, I haven’t gone out drinking that much, so I’m not exactly an expert.”
“You’re doing plenty good enough as it is.”
“Hmm… this really is something I can honestly call delicious. The taste just won’t leave my head.”
“Be careful now. It’s the same as with the food.”
“I know.”
“Well, as long as I’ve got the ingredients, I’ll make you some at dinner if I’ve got time to spare.”
“I’m grateful.”
“Vof.”

And so he chatted away with Crocodile Guy and Wolf. Incidentally, when I made a request in my usaunny form, Father made me an orange cocktail mixed with a boiled and mashed carrot-like vegetable. It was exquisite, indeed.
“Come to think of it, a lot of Filolials don’t really drink, huh.”
“I’m not too fond of the smell, personally.”
“There are some who do drink. They end up staggering about after having too much, I say.”

Chick used to drink, years later. There were others who liked to drink as well. Father remarked that there really were drunkard birds too, but they were quite rare. There was even one who’d shout as she chugged. For some reason, Father nicknamed her “Bird Bun.”
